title.title: Graph properties jump within $(\log n)^{-2}$
title.subtitle: Claim: symmetric monotone graph properties go from $\varepsilon$ to $1-\varepsilon$ in an edge-density window $O((\log n)^{-2})$

plain: Add random links one by one: a property like 'connected' flips from rare to near-certain in a sudden jump

beats.text: Schematic: a symmetric monotone graph property jumps from unlikely to likely
Friedgut–Kalai, 1996: the jump takes a window of width $O(1/\log n)$
The claim: width $(\log n)^{-2}$, the optimum they conjectured

steps: Freeze every edge outside a random block of about $\sqrt n$ vertices
Symmetry inside the block caps each edge's influence
That bounds the variance, so the jump happens in a narrow window

achievement.label: Friedgut–Kalai threshold-width conjecture (1996)
achievement.context: Bourgain–Kalai had $(\log n)^{-2+\eta}$ for every $\eta > 0$; the gain is removing $\eta$
achievement.note: The hypergraph companion, width $(\log n)^{-r/(r-1)}$, is not in Lean

verify.detail: In Lean: the graph case with the explicit constant $2^{19}$. Not the hypergraph theorem
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean statement; we did not build it

voice.text: Add random edges and properties flip from unlikely to likely. How narrow is the switch?
Freeze everything outside a random block; symmetry inside it caps every influence.
Claimed: width one over log n squared.

sources.ref: article, Sharp thresholds for graph properties
sources.quote: Friedgut and Kalai proved in 1996 that symmetric monotone graph properties have threshold width $O(1/\log n)$ and conjectured $(\log n)^{-2}$
